name: TeamStarWolf - Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 and ShinyHunters 2026 Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 case study: the ShinyHunters (UNC6240) zero-day wave of 27 May to 9 June 2026 against PeopleSoft PeopleTools, mostly in higher education, and the September 2026 n-day wave that got past WAF rules with an encoded path and planted JSP web shells. Score 100: a primary (Mandiant and GTIG, or ATT&CK's G1057 entry) states the behavior or lists the technique and the fit is direct. Score 60: the fit is partly inferred from a tool the primary names. Score 40: only a Reported source supports it. Scores measure the strength of the tie to this record, not severity. Comments carry the study's source numbers.

Exploit Public-Facing Application. CVE-2026-35273 in PeopleSoft PeopleTools: zero-day 27 May to 9 June 2026, n-day wave September 2026; listed by GTIG and mapped in ATT&CK's G1057 entry. Sources: [7] [8] [12].
Remote Access Tools. MeshCentral 1.1.59 in June 2026 and MeshAgent in May, July and September 2026; listed by GTIG in its 25 September 2026 report on the renewed campaign. Sources: [7] [8].
External Defacement. FBI recruitment site defaced, 22 September 2026, per news reporting (Reported). Sources: [15].
Web Shell. JSP web shells dropped into the PSEMHUB web application directory, repeated to reach every node behind a load balancer, September 2026; JSP hunting advised in June. Sources: [7] [8].
Pass the Hash. Pass-the-hash in a May 2026 breach later tied to the wave, per Sekoia and Beazley (Reported). Sources: [21].
Credentials In Files. Listed by GTIG in its 25 September 2026 report on the renewed campaign. Sources: [8].
Code Signing. SIDEEYE backdoor inside a trojanized, EV-signed media-player installer, September 2026; GTIG asked the CA to revoke the certificate. Sources: [8].
Archive via Utility. zstd used to archive data before exfiltration, June 2026; the binding is the study's reading of the tool GTIG names. Sources: [7].
Protocol Tunneling. Chisel tunnels in the same Beazley DFIR case (Reported). Sources: [21].
Exploits. ATT&CK's G1057 entry maps ShinyHunters' use of CVE-2026-35273 (zero-day window 27 May to 9 June 2026) to this technique. Sources: [12].
Digital Certificates. acme-client used to obtain certificates for a masquerading domain, June 2026; the binding is the study's reading of the tool GTIG names. Sources: [7].
Vulnerability Scanning. Roughly 5 to 15 verification probes per host before exploitation, September 2026; listed by GTIG in its 25 September 2026 report on the renewed campaign. Sources: [8].
Digital Certificates. Listed by GTIG in its 25 September 2026 report on the renewed campaign. Sources: [8].
Scan Databases. Listed by GTIG in its 25 September 2026 report on the renewed campaign. Sources: [8].
Financial Theft. Data-theft extortion: stolen data on the ShinyHunters leak site and a victim marker file, 9 June 2026. Sources: [7] [8] [12].
Disable or Modify Tools. EDR-disabling script in the same Beazley DFIR case (Reported). Sources: [21].
